correctness.rationale: For k,m>=1 set r=k+1, f=(1-x^2)^m, p_minus=sum_{j odd} binom(m,j)x^{2j}, p_plus=sum_{j even,j>=2}binom(m,j)x^{2j}. The radical-square-zero E-bimodule matrix N=p_plus I+p_minus(J-I) has nonnegative coefficients, no degree-zero radical and m positive degree-two arrows between every different pair, hence a connected finite-dimensional graded algebra. Its Cartan matrix I+N=f I+p_minus J is rationally similar to diagonal(f+r p_minus,f,...,f). At x=1+t the first factor has nonzero constant r*2^(m-1), remaining k factors have t-adic order exactly m, so Euler inverse has Smith profile (-m repeated k,0). This uses Q[[t]] for graded dimensions, independent of base-field characteristic. Independent symbolic matrix and determinant checks were performed at k,m=(1,1),(2,2),(3,3),(4,2).
